newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE GRAIN HARVEST GOING WELL-PRIME MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE GRAIN HARVEST GOING WELL-PRIME MINISTER.

text.p: Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko said on Wednesday that Ukraine expected a "much larger" grain harvest this year than last year's 25.4 million tonnes.
Officials have forecast a grain crop of 37-38 million tonnes in 1997 following much more agreeable weather conditions than the drought conditions of last year.
"So far this year's harvest is much bigger than it was last year. The harvest is going well," Pustovoitenko told a news conference.
"If the weather keeps up the way it is right now the harvest, for the first time in four years, will be gathered by August 19," he added.
General sunny conditions have replaced wet weather which soaked grain fields last month.
